purpose: The heading that opens a console page: an h1 whose `size` picks the heading token by page level, a one-line description, and the actions the page owns on the right. When the row runs out of room the actions move below the copy together; on a phone they stack, each at full width. It replaces the header markup every list, detail, settings and create page used to copy by hand.
useWhen: The top of any console page: a first-level list (`medium`), a detail tab or settings sub-page (`small`), a creation hub headline (`large`).
A page that owns actions (Documentation, a create action) that belong next to its title.
avoidWhen: The heading of one band inside a page → use `section-header`.
A settings band with a Hint and a card of rows → use `settings-section`.
related: section-header` — the h2 band heading inside a page.
page-tabs` — the second-level navigation strip that sits above a detail page's header.
button` — the usual content of the `actions` slot (outlined, `size="medium"`).
bestPractices: One PageHeader per page; it renders the page's only h1.
Put the Documentation link first and the create action on the outer edge, both outlined at the medium size.
Do not set `class="w-full"` on the action buttons; the header makes them full width on a phone.
Set `titleId` when a form or landmark names itself with `aria-labelledby`.
